streams.title: Account balances
streams.description: Authenticated balance updates for one root account or subaccount. JSON uses decimal amount strings; Protobuf uses unsigned 128-bit amount parts.

parameters.name: accountPublicId
parameters.description: Public root account or subaccount identifier authorized by the subscription token.

available.description: Spendable trading amount, computed as max(trading minus reserved, 0), in asset units as a decimal string with up to 18 fractional digits.

funding.description: Funding balance in asset units as a decimal string with up to 18 fractional digits.

fundingRevision.description: Opaque monotonic revision for the funding value. "0" means not yet observed.

reserved.description: Amount reserved from the trading balance in asset units as a decimal string with up to 18 fractional digits.

symbol.description: Unified asset symbol for these balances.

trading.description: Trading balance in asset units as a decimal string with up to 18 fractional digits.

tradingRevision.description: Opaque monotonic revision for the atomic trading, reserved, and available values. "0" means not yet observed.

streams.title: Ledger transfers
streams.description: Authenticated committed ledger transfer updates for one root account or subaccount. JSON uses decimal amount strings. Each publication is an ordered array of every event queued for the channel when it was sent, at most 256 events and 64 KiB: {"events":[…]} in JSON and ledger.read.v1.TransferRowBatch in protobuf. Apply events in array order and in publication order. (transferId, account, isDebit) identifies an event: an event whose identity was already received replaces the earlier copy, so a replayed or re-sent event is applied once. When the subscription reports that missed publications could not be recovered, reload recent transfers over REST.

parameters.name: accountPublicId
parameters.description: Public root account or subaccount identifier authorized by the subscription token.

events.description: Events in the stream's order, oldest first.

accountId.description: Public root-account or subaccount identifier when this side is safe to identify. Omitted for private or non-user sides.

address.description: External wallet or Polyester smart-account address when known and safe to expose. Omitted otherwise.

chainId.description: External network catalog identifier matching GetDepositWithdrawConfig chains[].chainId. Present only for EXTERNAL_ADDRESS.

kind.description: Side category: FUNDING_ACCOUNT, TRADING_ACCOUNT, EXTERNAL_ADDRESS, PRIVATE_COUNTERPARTY, FEE_ACCOUNT, or SYSTEM_ACCOUNT.

account.description: Lowercase account bucket affected by this row: funding or trading.

amount.description: Transferred amount in asset units as a decimal string with up to 18 fractional digits.

balanceAfter.description: Balance after this transfer in asset units as a decimal string with up to 18 fractional digits. Omitted when unavailable.

destination.description: Credit side of the transfer. Omitted when the side cannot be represented safely.

flowId.description: Public lifecycle flow identifier. Omitted when the transfer is not associated with a lifecycle flow.

isDebit.description: True when this row debits the subscribed account. Omitted for credit rows.

linkId.description: Identifier that groups related transfer legs, such as legs from one trade. Omitted when not applicable.

source.description: Debit side of the transfer. Omitted when the side cannot be represented safely.

symbol.description: Unified asset symbol for the transfer.

transferCode.description: Lowercase product reason for the transfer, such as deposit, withdraw, trade_base, trade_quote, internal_transfer, funding_to_trading, or trading_to_funding.

transferId.description: Stable transfer identifier, an unsigned 128-bit integer as a decimal string. Both legs of a transfer share it; with account and isDebit it identifies this leg.

streams.title: User trade executions
streams.description: Authenticated user trade executions for one root account or subaccount. JSON presents public identifiers, decimals, and RFC 3339 timestamps. Each publication is an ordered array of every event queued for the channel when it was sent, at most 256 events and 64 KiB: {"events":[…]} in JSON and orders.v1.UserTradeBatch in protobuf. Apply events in array order and in publication order. (matchId, orderId) identifies an event: an event whose identity was already received replaces the earlier copy, so a replayed or re-sent event is applied once. When the subscription reports that missed publications could not be recovered, reload recent fills over REST.

parameters.name: accountPublicId
parameters.description: Public root account or subaccount identifier authorized by the subscription token.

events.description: Events in the stream's order, oldest first.

executedAt.description: Fill execution time as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with up to nanosecond precision.

fee.description: Exact fee magnitude as a fixed 18-decimal string in the asset selected by feeAsset.

feeAsset.description: Asset charged or credited for the fee: QUOTE or BASE.

feeIsRebate.description: Whether this fill earned a rebate instead of paying a fee.

isMaker.description: True when this fill was the resting maker side; false for the taker side.

matchId.description: Monotonic match identifier within the symbol, encoded as an exact decimal string.

orderId.description: Public opaque identifier of the filled order.

price.description: Execution price in quote-asset units as a decimal string with up to nine fractional digits.

qty.description: Executed quantity in base-asset units as a decimal string using the market's configured quantity precision.

referralShare.description: Exact referral share as a fixed 18-decimal string in feeAsset. Zero when none was allocated.

side.description: Filled order side: BUY or SELL.

symbol.description: Spot trading pair symbol, for example BTC-USDT.

streams.title: Trigger events
streams.description: Authenticated spot trigger activation, fire, update, cancellation, and failure events for one root account or subaccount. Each publication is an ordered array of every event queued for the channel when it was sent, at most 256 events and 64 KiB: {"events":[…]} in JSON and triggers.v1.TriggerEventBatch in protobuf. Apply events in array order and in publication order. (triggerId, eventType, childSeq, tsNs) identifies an event: an event whose identity was already received replaces the earlier copy, so a replayed or re-sent event is applied once. When the subscription reports that missed publications could not be recovered, reload recent trigger events over REST. Enum values here use their full protobuf names, as ConnectRPC does, for example EVENT_CANCELED and TRIGGER_CANCEL_REASON_USER_REQUEST; REST returns the same values without the prefix, for example CANCELED and USER_REQUEST.

parameters.name: accountPublicId
parameters.description: Public root account or subaccount identifier authorized by the subscription token.

events.description: Events in the stream's order, oldest first.

cancelReason.description: TriggerCancelReason enum name. Present only for EVENT_CANCELED.

childOrderId.description: Public identifier of the child order created by this event. Omitted when no child was created.

childSeq.description: Child sequence number for multi-child trigger strategies. Zero when not applicable.

eventType.description: Event category: EVENT_ACTIVATED, EVENT_ARMED, EVENT_FIRED, EVENT_FIRE_REFUSED, EVENT_CANCELED, EVENT_UPDATED, or EVENT_FAILED.

failureReason.description: TriggerFailureReason enum name. Present only for EVENT_FAILED.

firePx.description: Price that fired the trigger: for a stop-loss or take-profit, the price that crossed its trigger price; for a trailing stop, its trailing trigger threshold when it fired; for a ladder, the level's price. A market child order's slippage cap is measured from it. In quote-asset units as a decimal string with up to nine fractional digits. Zero for non-firing events, including EVENT_ACTIVATED and EVENT_ARMED. For EVENT_FIRE_REFUSED, the price the refused attempt fired at.

fireRefusalReason.description: TriggerFailureReason enum name of the refused attempt named by childSeq. Present only for EVENT_FIRE_REFUSED, which leaves the trigger live.

subaccountId.description: Public root-account or subaccount identifier associated with the trigger.

symbol.description: Spot trading pair symbol of the trigger, for example BTC-USDT.

triggerType.description: Trigger type: STOP_LOSS, TAKE_PROFIT, TRAILING_STOP, TWAP, or LADDER.

tsNs.description: Event time in Unix nanoseconds (UTC), encoded as an exact decimal string.

streams.title: Zipped asset supply
streams.description: Public batched supply updates for zipped-asset routes: each new supply reading, and one STALE update when a route's supply stops being refreshed. Every update carries its status and the time its supply was read from Polyester chain. JSON uses decimal strings; Protobuf uses scaled integers. Read the initial state of every route, including routes with no known supply, from the deposit and withdraw config.

updates.description: Latest absolute supply values for the zipped-asset routes changed in this batch; entries are not deltas.

observedAt.description: When the supply was read from Polyester chain, as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp.

status.description: AVAILABLE when the supply is current; STALE when it has not been refreshed for longer than expected and may no longer be accurate.

supply.description: Latest zToken supply for the route in unified-asset units as a decimal string using the asset's configured quantity precision. '0' is a real supply of zero.

zippedAssetId.description: Canonical numeric identifier of the zipped-asset route.

streams.title: Current candles
streams.description: Public current-candle updates for one timeframe and spot symbol. JSON uses decimal strings. Protobuf uses scaled integers: prices at scale 9, and volume at the base asset's market_data_volume_scale from GetSpotConfig (8 in the example).

parameters.name: timeframe
parameters.description: Candle interval: 1s, 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 2h, 4h, 6h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d, 1w, or 1mo. Buckets are UTC: up to 1d they start on whole multiples of their length since midnight, 3d buckets start every third day from 1970-01-01, 1w buckets start on Monday, and 1mo buckets start on the first day of the month.

parameters.name: symbolId
parameters.description: Numeric spot market symbol identifier.

close.description: Latest or closing price in quote-asset units as a decimal string with up to nine fractional digits.

high.description: Highest price in the bucket, including the open, in quote-asset units as a decimal string with up to nine fractional digits.

isClosed.description: True only for the terminal update emitted after the bucket closes; false for updates to the current open bucket.

low.description: Lowest price in the bucket, including the open, in quote-asset units as a decimal string with up to nine fractional digits.

open.description: Opening price in quote-asset units as a decimal string with up to nine fractional digits: the previous candle's close, or the first trade for a market's first candle.

quoteVolume.description: Exact traded quote-asset volume in the bucket as a decimal string: the sum of execution price times execution quantity, not close times volume.

tsSec.description: Candle bucket start time in Unix seconds (UTC), encoded as an exact decimal string.

volume.description: Traded base-asset quantity in the bucket as a decimal string with up to 18 fractional digits.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Heatmap interval: 1s, 1m, 5m, or 1h.

parameters.name: symbolId
parameters.description: Numeric spot market symbol identifier.

streams.title: Price band
streams.description: One spot pair's live price band: its reference price and the limit prices the pair admits, the same band GetPriceBand returns. A changed band is sent at once, and while the band stays current, an unchanged band is sent again about every 2 seconds, so validUntil stays ahead. When no band was confirmed within the last 5 seconds, the stream sends the band once with state UNKNOWN, without prices, and nothing more until the band returns; GetPriceBand refuses with PRICE_BAND_STALE or PRICE_BAND_UNKNOWN in the same case. A band whose validUntil has passed is unknown too. UNKNOWN carries the epoch, updateId and asOf of the last confirmation of the band it replaces. Each message replaces the previous one; when a message is repeated or arrives late, keep the one with the greatest epoch, then updateId, then asOf, and at an equal one keep UNKNOWN. A new subscription receives no earlier message: read GetPriceBand, or, while the band stays current, wait about 2 seconds for the next one. A reconnecting client recovers the messages it missed while the channel's history still holds them. JSON carries GetPriceBand's REST body, protobuf a marketdata.v1.GetPriceBandResponse.

parameters.name: symbolId
parameters.description: Numeric spot market symbol identifier.

band.description: The pair's price band. Its state is UNKNOWN when no band was confirmed within the last 5 seconds.

asOf.description: When the band was last confirmed current.

epoch.description: The band's epoch, an unsigned 64-bit decimal string. It never decreases, and a band of a greater epoch is newer. Compare updateId only within one epoch.

maxBuyPrice.description: The highest buy limit price admitted, inclusive, as a decimal string. Present only when state is ACTIVE.

maxSellPrice.description: The highest sell limit price admitted, inclusive, as a decimal string. Present only when state is ACTIVE and the band limits passive prices too.

minBuyPrice.description: The lowest buy limit price admitted, inclusive, as a decimal string. Present only when state is ACTIVE and the band limits passive prices too.

minSellPrice.description: The lowest sell limit price admitted, inclusive, as a decimal string. Present only when state is ACTIVE.

parameters.description: The band's settings, as GetSpotConfig returns them. Absent when the state is OFF, or when the settings in effect cannot be expressed exactly in basis points and milliseconds; the limits above are authoritative either way.

lowerBps.description: How far below the reference price a sell may be priced or trade, in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). The lower limit is the reference price times (1 - lower_bps / 10000), rounded up to the tick size.

referenceWindowMs.description: How long the reference price stays fixed before it can move to a newer trade, in milliseconds. Zero moves it with every order.

upperBps.description: How far above the reference price a buy may be priced or trade, in basis points. The upper limit is the reference price times (1 + upper_bps / 10000), rounded down to the tick size.

reanchorEligibleAt.description: From when the next order operation on the pair may move the reference price. Nothing moves at that time by itself. Present when state is ACTIVE or EMPTY.

reanchorPending.description: True when a trade newer than the reference price is waiting: once the re-anchor eligibility time has passed, the next order operation moves the reference to it, unless the index price moves it instead. False does not promise that the band stays: a move to the index price needs no trade.

referencePrice.description: The band's reference price as a decimal string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example '61000.25'. Present when state is ACTIVE or EMPTY.

referenceSource.description: Where the reference price came from. REFERENCE_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED when the state is OFF or UNKNOWN.

symbol.description: The pair's symbol, for example BTC-USDT.

updateId.description: Increases with each band update within an epoch, and may increase without one, as an unsigned 64-bit decimal string. Compare it only within one epoch: a greater value is newer.

updatedAt.description: When the band last changed: its first setting, OFF included, a change of its settings, or a move of its reference price, to the same price included.

validUntil.description: asOf plus 5 seconds. After it, treat the band as unknown and read it again.

streams.title: Market trades
streams.description: Public executed spot trades for one symbol, in execution order. JSON presents decimal amounts and an RFC 3339 execution timestamp. Each publication is an ordered array of every event queued for the channel when it was sent, at most 256 events and 64 KiB: {"events":[…]} in JSON and marketdata.v1.MarketTradeBatch in protobuf. Apply events in array order and in publication order. matchId identifies an event: an event whose identity was already received replaces the earlier copy, so a replayed or re-sent event is applied once. When the subscription reports that missed publications could not be recovered, reload recent trades over REST.

parameters.name: symbolId
parameters.description: Numeric spot market symbol identifier.

events.description: Events in the stream's order, oldest first.

executedAt.description: Trade execution time as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC with up to nanosecond precision.

matchId.description: Monotonic trade identifier within the symbol, encoded as an exact decimal string.

price.description: Trade price in quote-asset units as a decimal string with up to nine fractional digits.

qty.description: Traded quantity in base-asset units as a decimal string using the market's configured quantity precision.

side.description: Taker or aggressor side: BUY when the taker bought the base asset, otherwise SELL.

symbol.description: Spot trading pair symbol, for example BTC-USDT.

streams.title: Orderbook deltas
streams.description: Public spot orderbook SET-style updates for one symbol and depth tier. Each update is the difference between two published views of the tier's top levels per side. A reset update carrying the full view arrives periodically, currently about every 30 seconds, and after a sequence gap. To start, subscribe at a streamed tier, then fetch the orderbook snapshot API at exactly that tier: drop updates whose bookSeqEnd is at most the snapshot's bookSeq, and apply the first update only when its bookSeqStart equals that bookSeq. Otherwise, or after a gap, wait for the next reset.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Streamed depth tier, in levels per side. Supported values are 1, 20, 50, 200, and 500. They are the streamed subset of the depth tiers the orderbook snapshot API serves, which also include 5, 10, 100, 1000 and 5000. A subscription at any other depth is refused with error code 107 (bad request).

parameters.name: symbolId
parameters.description: Numeric spot market symbol identifier.

asks.description: Ask-side SET updates as [price, quantity] decimal-string tuples. A zero quantity removes the price level from this tier's view. Omitted when no ask levels changed.

prefixItems.description: Price in quote-asset units with up to nine fractional digits.
Quantity in base-asset units using the market's configured precision; zero removes the level from this tier's view.

bids.description: Bid-side SET updates as [price, quantity] decimal-string tuples. A zero quantity removes the price level from this tier's view. Omitted when no bid levels changed.

prefixItems.description: Price in quote-asset units with up to nine fractional digits.
Quantity in base-asset units using the market's configured precision; zero removes the level from this tier's view.

bookSeqEnd.description: Book sequence of the view after this update. It can advance without any change to the book.

bookSeqStart.description: Book sequence of the view this update applies to: the previous update's bookSeqEnd. Apply it only to a book at exactly this sequence. 0 when reset is true.

reset.description: When true, clear the local book before applying this message; the level arrays contain the current view for the subscribed depth tier.

ts.description: Best-effort timestamp associated with the book update in Unix milliseconds (UTC). Omitted when unavailable.
